e-4097.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Solutions of Exponential Equations
e-4097.problem: Expressed in terms of $\log_2,$ what value of $x$ satisfies the equation $2^{x+1}=3^x?$
e-4097.worked_solution:
First, we take $\log_2$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{x+1} & ={3}^{x} \\ {log}_{2}⁡({2}^{x+1}) & ={log}_{2}⁡({3}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\log_b \left( b^c \right) = c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+1 = \log_2 \left(3^{x}\right)
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x+1 = x \log_2 \left(3\right)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =x{log}_{2}⁡(3) \\ x{log}_{2}⁡(3)-x & =1 \\ x({log}_{2}⁡(3)-1) & =1 \\ x & =\frac{1}{{log}_{2}⁡(3)-1}\end{aligned}
$$

e-4098.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions of Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm
e-4098.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation $e^{x+1}=2^x\cdot 5?$
e-4098.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+1} & ={2}^{x}\cdot 5 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x+1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x}\cdot 5)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+1 =\ln \left(2^{x}\cdot 5\right)
$$

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x+1 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-1 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-1 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-1}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\end{aligned}
$$

e-18776.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions of Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm: Advanced Cases
e-18776.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, determine the value of $x$ that satisfies the equation $5^{x+2}=9^{x-2}.$
e-18776.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{x+2} & ={9}^{x-2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x+2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({9}^{x-2})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
(x+2)\ln(5) = (x-2)\ln(9).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =(x-2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)) & =2(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)) \\ x & =\frac{2(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(9))}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Expressed in terms of log4, what value of x satisfies the equation 4x+1=7x?

a
1−log4⁡(7)
b
1+log4⁡(7)log4⁡(7)
c
log4⁡(7)1−log4⁡(7)
d
−11−log4⁡(7)
e
log4⁡(7)−1
Submit

decision.explanation: Taking log base 4 gives x+1=x\log_4(7). Thus x(\log_4(7)-1)=1, so x=1/(\log_4(7)-1)=-1/(1-\log_4(7)), which is option d.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Expressed in terms of ${log}_{4}$, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${4}^{x+1}={7}^{x}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{4}$ in both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{x+1} & ={7}^{x} \\ {log}_{4}⁡({4}^{x+1}) & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{4}⁡({4}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x}) \\ x+1 & =x{log}_{4}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =x{log}_{4}⁡(7) \\ x-x{log}_{4}⁡(7) & =-1 \\ x(1-{log}_{4}⁡(7)) & =-1 \\ x & =-\frac{1}{1-{log}_{4}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Expressed in terms of log4, what value of x satisfies the equation 4x+1=7x?

a
1−log4⁡(7)
b
1+log4⁡(7)log4⁡(7)
c
log4⁡(7)1−log4⁡(7)
d
−11−log4⁡(7)
e
log4⁡(7)−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we take log4 in both sides of the equation: 4x+1=7xlog4⁡(4x+1)=log4⁡(7x)

Now, we use the fact that log4⁡(4c)=c to simplify the left-hand side. This gives: x+1=log4⁡(7x)

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side: x+1=log4⁡(7x)x+1=xlog4⁡(7)

Finally, we solve for x, as follows: x+1=xlog4⁡(7)x−xlog4⁡(7)=−1x(1−log4⁡(7))=−1x=−11−log4⁡(7)

content.problem: Expressed in terms of ${log}_{4}$, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${4}^{x+1}={7}^{x}?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{4}$ in both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{x+1} & ={7}^{x} \\ {log}_{4}⁡({4}^{x+1}) & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{4}⁡({4}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & ={log}_{4}⁡({7}^{x}) \\ x+1 & =x{log}_{4}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =x{log}_{4}⁡(7) \\ x-x{log}_{4}⁡(7) & =-1 \\ x(1-{log}_{4}⁡(7)) & =-1 \\ x & =-\frac{1}{1-{log}_{4}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we take the common logarithm $(log)$ of both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{10}^{x+1} & ={2}^{x} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{x+1}) & =\operatorname{log}⁡({2}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+1=\operatorname{log}⁡({2}^{x})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x+1=x\operatorname{log}⁡(2)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{log}⁡(2)-x & =1 \\ x(\operatorname{log}⁡(2)-1) & =1 \\ x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{log}⁡(2)-1}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Given that ${5}^{y}={4}^{y+1},$ what is the value of $y?$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
after.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{5}$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{y}={4}^{y+1} \\ {log}_{5}⁡({5}^{y}) & ={log}_{5}⁡({4}^{y+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={log}_{5}⁡({4}^{y+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(y+1){log}_{5}⁡4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(y+1){log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y & =y{log}_{5}⁡4+{log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y-y{log}_{5}⁡4 & ={log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y(1-{log}_{5}⁡4) & ={log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y & =\frac{{log}_{5}⁡4}{1-{log}_{5}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the change of base formula, we have

$$
{log}_{5}⁡(4)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}≈0.861\,353.
$$

Finally, then, we can approximate $y$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}y≈\frac{0.861\,353}{1-0.861\,353}≈6.213,\end{aligned}
$$

to $3$ decimal places.

Question 3
?

Given that 5y=4y+1, what is the value of y? Round your answer to 3 decimal places.

a
6.213
b
−5.891
c
0.544
d
1.293
e
7.712
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we take log5 on both sides of the equation:

5y=4y+1log5⁡(5y)=log5⁡(4y+1)

Now, we use the fact that logb⁡(bc)=c to simplify the left-hand side:

y=log5⁡(4y+1)

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

y=(y+1)log5⁡4

Finally, we solve for y, as follows:

y=(y+1)log5⁡4y=ylog5⁡4+log5⁡4y−ylog5⁡4=log5⁡4y(1−log5⁡4)=log5⁡4y=log5⁡41−log5⁡4

Using the change of base formula, we have

log5⁡(4)=ln⁡(4)ln⁡(5)≈0.861353.

Finally, then, we can approximate y as

y≈0.8613531−0.861353≈6.213, to 3 decimal places.

content.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Solutions of Exponential Equations
content.problem: Given that ${5}^{y}={4}^{y+1},$ what is the value of $y?$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
content.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{5}$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{y}={4}^{y+1} \\ {log}_{5}⁡({5}^{y}) & ={log}_{5}⁡({4}^{y+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={log}_{5}⁡({4}^{y+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(y+1){log}_{5}⁡4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(y+1){log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y & =y{log}_{5}⁡4+{log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y-y{log}_{5}⁡4 & ={log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y(1-{log}_{5}⁡4) & ={log}_{5}⁡4 \\ y & =\frac{{log}_{5}⁡4}{1-{log}_{5}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the change of base formula, we have

$$
{log}_{5}⁡(4)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}≈0.861\,353.
$$

Finally, then, we can approximate $y$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}y≈\frac{0.861\,353}{1-0.861\,353}≈6.213,\end{aligned}
$$

to $3$ decimal places.

Question 4
?

Expressed in terms of common logarithms, what value of x satisfies the equation 10x−3=7x?

a
1−log⁡(7)
b
3log⁡(7)
c
−3log⁡(7)
d
31−log⁡(7)
e
11+2log⁡(7)
Submit

decision.explanation: Taking common logarithms gives x-3=x log(7). Thus x(1-log(7))=3, so x=3/(1-log(7)), which is option d.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Expressed in terms of common logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${10}^{x-3}={7}^{x}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we take the common logarithm $(log)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{10}^{x-3} & ={7}^{x} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{x-3}) & =\operatorname{log}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =\operatorname{log}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =x\operatorname{log}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-x\operatorname{log}⁡(7) & =3 \\ x(1-\operatorname{log}⁡(7)) & =3 \\ x & =\frac{3}{1-\operatorname{log}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Expressed in terms of common logarithms, what value of x satisfies the equation 10x−3=7x?

a
1−log⁡(7)
b
3log⁡(7)
c
−3log⁡(7)
d
31−log⁡(7)
e
11+2log⁡(7)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we take the common logarithm (log) of both sides of the equation:

10x−3=7xlog⁡(10x−3)=log⁡(7x)

Now, we use the fact that logb⁡(bc)=c to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

x−3=log⁡(7x)

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

x−3=xlog⁡(7)

Finally, we solve for x, as follows:

x−xlog⁡(7)=3x(1−log⁡(7))=3x=31−log⁡(7)

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms x-3=x log(7), so x(1-log(7))=3 and x=3/(1-log(7)). Thus option d is correct; the deliberately submitted option e is incorrect.

content.problem: Expressed in terms of common logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${10}^{x-3}={7}^{x}?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we take the common logarithm $(log)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{10}^{x-3} & ={7}^{x} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{x-3}) & =\operatorname{log}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =\operatorname{log}⁡({7}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =x\operatorname{log}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-x\operatorname{log}⁡(7) & =3 \\ x(1-\operatorname{log}⁡(7)) & =3 \\ x & =\frac{3}{1-\operatorname{log}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$

x≈

decision.explanation: Taking logarithms gives (1-x)ln(8)=(x/2)ln(3). Solving yields x=ln(8)/(ln(8)+ln(3)/2)≈0.791039, which rounds to 0.791.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{8}$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{8}^{1-x} & ={3}^{x/2} \\ {log}_{8}⁡({8}^{1-x}) & ={log}_{8}⁡({3}^{x/2})\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

$$
1-x={log}_{8}⁡({3}^{x/2})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
1-x=\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-x & =\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3 \\ 1 & =x+\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3 \\ x+\frac{x}{2}{log}_{8}⁡3 & =1 \\ 2x+x{log}_{8}⁡3 & =2 \\ x(2+{log}_{8}⁡3) & =2 \\ x & =\frac{2}{2+{log}_{8}⁡3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the change of base formula, we have

$$
{log}_{8}⁡(3)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}≈0.528\,321.
$$

Finally,  we can approximate $x$ as 

$$
x≈\frac{2}{2+0.528\,321}≈0.791,
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $y$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{y}={8}^{1-2y}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{y} & ={8}^{1-2y} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({8}^{1-2y})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡({8}^{1-2y})
$$

Finally, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
y=(1-2y)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)
$$

Finally, we solve for $y$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(1-2y)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)-2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ y+2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ y(1+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ y & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}{1+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $y$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{y+1}={3}^{2y}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{y+1} & ={3}^{2y} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y+1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2y})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
y+1=\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2y})\,
$$

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
y+1=2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)
$$

Finally, we solve for $y$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y+1 & =2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ 2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-y & =1 \\ y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-1) & =1 \\ y & =\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-1}\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 8
?

Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of x satisfies the equation ex−3=5x+1?

a
ln⁡51+ln⁡5
b
−ln⁡5+1ln⁡5
c
ln⁡5+31−ln⁡5
d
ln⁡5−11+ln⁡5
e
ln⁡5+3ln⁡5
Submit

decision.explanation: Taking natural logarithms gives x-3=(x+1)ln(5). Rearranging gives x(1-ln(5))=ln(5)+3, so option c is correct.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{x-3}={5}^{x+1}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x-3} & ={5}^{x+1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x-3}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x-3=\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x+1})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x-3=(x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =(x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x-3 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡5+3 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡5+3 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+3}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we take the natural logarithm (ln) of both sides of the equation:

ex−3=5x+1ln⁡(ex−3)=ln⁡(5x+1)

Now, we use the fact that ln⁡(ea)=a to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

x−3=ln⁡(5x+1)

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

x−3=(x+1)ln⁡5

content.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{x-3}={5}^{x+1}?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x-3} & ={5}^{x+1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x-3}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x-3=\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x+1})
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x-3=(x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-3 & =(x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x-3 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡5+\operatorname{ln}⁡5 \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡5+3 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡5+3 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5+3}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution of 32x=81−6x.

a
2ln⁡(3)+ln⁡(8)ln⁡(3)−ln⁡(8)
b
ln⁡(8)2(ln⁡(3)+3ln⁡(8))
c
3ln⁡(3)+ln⁡(8)
d
2ln⁡(8)
e
12(ln⁡(3)+3ln⁡(8))

decision.explanation: Taking natural logarithms gives 2x ln(3)=(1-6x)ln(8). Thus x(2ln(3)+6ln(8))=ln(8), so x=ln(8)/(2(ln(3)+3ln(8))), option b.

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{2x} & ={8}^{1-6x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({8}^{1-6x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(1-6x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(1-6x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)-6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 2x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}{2(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8))}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Find the solution of 32x=81−6x.

a
2ln⁡(3)+ln⁡(8)ln⁡(3)−ln⁡(8)
b
ln⁡(8)2(ln⁡(3)+3ln⁡(8))
c
3ln⁡(3)+ln⁡(8)
d
2ln⁡(8)
e
12(ln⁡(3)+3ln⁡(8))
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we take the natural logarithm (ln) of both sides of the equation:

32x=81−6xln⁡(32x)=ln⁡(81−6x)

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

2xln⁡(3)=(1−6x)ln⁡(8)

Finally, we solve for x, as follows:

2xln⁡(3)=(1−6x)ln⁡(8)2xln⁡(3)=ln⁡(8)−6xln⁡(8)2xln⁡(3)+6xln⁡(8)=ln⁡(8)2x(ln⁡(3)+3ln⁡(8))=ln⁡(8)x=ln⁡(8)2(ln⁡(3)+3ln⁡(8))

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms 2x ln(3)=(1-6x)ln(8), so 2x(ln(3)+3ln(8))=ln(8). Therefore option b is correct; the deliberately submitted option d is incorrect.

content.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{2x} & ={8}^{1-6x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({8}^{1-6x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(1-6x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(1-6x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)-6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 2x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}{2(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8))}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

Find the solution of 3x+5=76−2x.

a
6ln⁡(3)+5ln⁡(7)ln⁡(7)−ln⁡(3)
b
1ln⁡(3)+2ln⁡(7)
c
6ln⁡(7)ln⁡(3)ln⁡(3)+2ln⁡(7)
d
6ln⁡(7)−5ln⁡(3)ln⁡(3)+2ln⁡(7)
e
16ln⁡(7)−5ln⁡(3)
Submit

decision.explanation: Taking natural logarithms gives (x+5)ln(3)=(6-2x)ln(7). Collecting x terms yields x(ln(3)+2ln(7))=6ln(7)-5ln(3), so option d is correct.

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{x+5} & ={7}^{6-2x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{x+5}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{6-2x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(6-2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(6-2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x & =\frac{6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

Find the solution of 3x+5=76−2x.

a
6ln⁡(3)+5ln⁡(7)ln⁡(7)−ln⁡(3)
b
1ln⁡(3)+2ln⁡(7)
c
6ln⁡(7)ln⁡(3)ln⁡(3)+2ln⁡(7)
d
6ln⁡(7)−5ln⁡(3)ln⁡(3)+2ln⁡(7)
e
16ln⁡(7)−5ln⁡(3)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we take the natural logarithm (ln) of both sides of the equation:

3x+5=76−2xln⁡(3x+5)=ln⁡(76−2x)

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

(x+5)ln⁡(3)=(6−2x)ln⁡(7)

Finally, we solve for x, as follows:

(x+5)ln⁡(3)=(6−2x)ln⁡(7)xln⁡(3)+5ln⁡(3)=6ln⁡(7)−2xln⁡(7)xln⁡(3)+2xln⁡(7)=6ln⁡(7)−5ln⁡(3)x(ln⁡(3)+2ln⁡(7))=6ln⁡(7)−5ln⁡(3)x=6ln⁡(7)−5ln⁡(3)ln⁡(3)+2ln⁡(7)

content.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{x+5} & ={7}^{6-2x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{x+5}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{6-2x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(6-2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(6-2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x & =\frac{6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Find the solution of 4x+7=58−4x.

a
1ln⁡(4)+4ln⁡(5)
b
−8ln⁡(5)+ln⁡(4)ln⁡(4)+2ln⁡(5)
c
18ln⁡(5)−7ln⁡(4)
d
8ln⁡(5)−ln⁡(4)ln⁡(4)−4ln⁡(5)
e
8ln⁡(5)−7ln⁡(4)ln⁡(4)+4ln⁡(5)
Submit

decision.explanation: Taking natural logarithms gives (x+7)ln(4)=(8-4x)ln(5). Therefore x(ln(4)+4ln(5))=8ln(5)-7ln(4), so option e is correct.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{x+7} & ={5}^{8-4x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{x+7}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{8-4x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+7)\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =(8-4x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+7)\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =(8-4x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+7\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ x & =\frac{8\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Find the solution of 4x+7=58−4x.

a
1ln⁡(4)+4ln⁡(5)
b
−8ln⁡(5)+ln⁡(4)ln⁡(4)+2ln⁡(5)
c
18ln⁡(5)−7ln⁡(4)
d
8ln⁡(5)−ln⁡(4)ln⁡(4)−4ln⁡(5)
e
8ln⁡(5)−7ln⁡(4)ln⁡(4)+4ln⁡(5)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we take the natural logarithm (ln) of both sides of the equation:

4x+7=58−4xln⁡(4x+7)=ln⁡(58−4x)

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

(x+7)ln⁡(4)=(8−4x)ln⁡(5)

Finally, we solve for x, as follows:

(x+7)ln⁡(4)=(8−4x)ln⁡(5)xln⁡(4)+7ln⁡(4)=8ln⁡(5)−4xln⁡(5)xln⁡(4)+4xln⁡(5)=8ln⁡(5)−7ln⁡(4)x(ln⁡(4)+4ln⁡(5))=8ln⁡(5)−7ln⁡(4)x=8ln⁡(5)−7ln⁡(4)ln⁡(4)+4ln⁡(5)

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms (x+7)ln(4)=(8-4x)ln(5), giving x(ln(4)+4ln(5))=8ln(5)-7ln(4). Thus option e is correct; the deliberately submitted option c is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions of Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm: Advanced Cases
content.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{x+7} & ={5}^{8-4x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{x+7}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{8-4x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+7)\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =(8-4x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+7)\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =(8-4x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+7\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ x & =\frac{8\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Find the solution of 2x+3=98−5x.

a
1ln⁡(2)+5ln⁡(9)
b
8ln⁡(9)−ln⁡(2)ln⁡(2)−3ln⁡(9)
c
8ln⁡(9)−3ln⁡(2)ln⁡(2)+5ln⁡(9)
d
8ln⁡(9)+ln⁡(2)ln⁡(9)−5ln⁡(2)
e
18ln⁡(9)−3ln⁡(2)
Submit

decision.explanation: Taking natural logarithms gives (x+3)ln(2)=(8-5x)ln(9). Hence x(ln(2)+5ln(9))=8ln(9)-3ln(2), so option c is correct.

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{x+3} & ={9}^{8-5x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+3}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({9}^{8-5x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =(8-5x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =(8-5x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-5x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+5x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x & =\frac{8\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)}\end{aligned}
$$

a

EXPLANATION

First, we take the natural logarithm (ln) of both sides of the equation:

2x+3=98−5xln⁡(2x+3)=ln⁡(98−5x)

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

(x+3)ln⁡(2)=(8−5x)ln⁡(9)

Finally, we solve for x, as follows:

(x+3)ln⁡(2)=(8−5x)ln⁡(9)xln⁡(2)+3ln⁡(2)=8ln⁡(9)−5xln⁡(9)xln⁡(2)+5xln⁡(9)=8ln⁡(9)−3ln⁡(2)x(ln⁡(2)+5ln⁡(9))=8ln⁡(9)−3ln⁡(2)x=8ln⁡(9)−3ln⁡(2)ln⁡(2)+5ln⁡(9)

content.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{x+3} & ={9}^{8-5x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+3}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({9}^{8-5x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =(8-5x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =(8-5x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-5x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+5x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x & =\frac{8\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)}\end{aligned}
$$
